title: pkix-dane-resolver: TTL-respecting TLSA cache
description:
## Why

TLSA records carry DNS TTLs and the same (host, port, proto) is queried on every connection to that service, so caching is an expected deployment pattern rather than an optimization. PKIX-j32w.2 shipped without one deliberately: AGENTS.md non-negotiable #6 requires the workspace to ADMIT caches, not build them, and AsyncTlsaResolver is already shaped for a wrapper -- &self receivers, and a TlsaResponse that is Clone + PartialEq and serde-serializable behind a feature.

Hickory's own response cache applies underneath, so this is not a total absence of caching today. What is missing is a cache at the TlsaResponse layer, which is what a consumer can inspect, persist and share.

## Shape

A wrapper rather than a change to HickoryTlsaResolver, so a caller can wrap any AsyncTlsaResolver including their own:

    pub struct CachingTlsaResolver<R> { inner: R, ... }
    impl<R: AsyncTlsaResolver> AsyncTlsaResolver for CachingTlsaResolver<R>

## Decide before building

- Where the TTL comes from. TlsaResponse does NOT currently carry one: pkix-dane's type has records and a DnssecStatus and nothing else. Either add a TTL to TlsaResponse (a pkix-dane change, breaking) or have the resolver return it alongside. Resolve this first; it is the only part that reaches into another crate.
- Whether negative answers are cached, and for how long. A signed NODATA is a durable fact and worth caching; an Indeterminate result usually means something transient and probably is not.
- Whether Bogus is cached at all. Caching a Bogus verdict lets a transient attack or misconfiguration persist past its cause; not caching it means a sustained attack costs a lookup every time. Lean toward not caching Bogus.
- Bounds. An unbounded cache keyed on caller-supplied names is a memory-growth vector when the caller validates many hosts. Needs a cap and an eviction policy.

## Acceptance

[ ] TTL source decided and recorded
[ ] Wrapper implements AsyncTlsaResolver over any inner resolver
[ ] Entries expire per TTL; expiry is tested without sleeping on a real clock
[ ] Negative and Bogus caching policy decided, recorded, and tested
[ ] Bounded, with a documented eviction policy
